result.title: From Spectral to Frobenius: When Muon Loses Its Spectral Implicit Bias
result.summary: Prior work on implicit bias shows that gradient descent selects the Frobenius max-margin direction on linearly separable problems, whereas Fan et al. (2025) established spectral max-margin behavior for spectral-norm steepest descent methods, including idealized Muon with exact orthogonalization. In practice, however, Muon approximates orthogonalization using finite Newton-Schulz iterations and a positive stabilization constant. We prove that these implementation choices cause Muon to select the Frobenius rather than the spectral max-margin direction in linear classification with separable data. We also establish this behavior for both exponential moving average and Nesterov-style momentum. The key technical ingredient is a summable perturbation argument showing that the resulting parameter trajectories remain at bounded distance from those of gradient descent. We then disentangle the roles of Newton-Schulz iteration count, the stabilization constant, and the Newton-Schulz polynomial, revealing distinct asymptotic behaviors, including directions that achieve neither Frobenius nor spectral max-margin. Finally, we show that Muon can recover its spectral max-margin bias with Newton-Schulz iterations growing logarithmically over training.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 Muon 优化器的隐式偏置：证明有限 Newton-Schulz 迭代与稳定常数使 Muon 在线性可分分类中趋向 Frobenius 而非 spectral 最大间隔方向，并在动量下保持该结论，而当迭代次数随训练对数增长时可恢复 spectral 偏置。
